case.question: Propose a launch menu for both Dubai and Abu Dhabi, with portions and localization.
expected: Meaty pizza and kebab sandwich identity retained
Portions and adaptations explained as proposals

answer.headline: One shared core menu, with small city-level tweaks: Jordanian meat pizza and kebab sandwiches as hero items, sized for delivery, priced as test bands pending cost validation.

sections.title: Menu architecture to launch (shared core, Dubai + Abu Dhabi)

items.text: Keep the concept tight: two hero categories only. Suggested launch list - (1) Jordanian meat pizza: spiced minced-beef/lamb 'arayes-style' base with tahini, sumac onions, pine nuts; (2) kebab sandwich: charcoal-grilled kofta or chicken kebab in saj/taboon flatbread with garlic toum, pickles, tomato, parsley. This preserves the core products in the profile rather than spreading into generic Lebanese or fried-chicken ranges.

Observed comparable portions and size laddering in these cities: a Dubai JBR delivery menu lists a chicken/falafel sandwich range where regular is AED 13 and large AED 18 (falafel), and a Khalifa City (Abu Dhabi) menu lists a shawarma size ladder of small AED 11, regular AED 15.50, large AED 26. Pizza is also sold by inch size: a UAE-wide chain web menu lists one 8in / 10in / 13in ladder at AED 33 / 50 / 69.

Proposal: mirror that size logic rather than inventing a new one - kebab sandwich in regular and large, and meat pizza in 8in personal, 10in sharing and 13in family formats. Proposed portions (to be weighed, not asserted): regular sandwich ~220-250g total with ~100-120g cooked kebab; large ~330-380g; pizza 8in ~28-30cm-class dough ball ~180-200g, 13in ~300-330g. These are starting specifications to be set on a scale in your own kitchen, not observed market weights - the cited competitor listings did not publish gram weights or pizza diameters.

Dubai: keep English/Arabic menu naming with transliterated Jordanian terms (arayes, kofta kebab, saj) and a short provenance line ('Jordanian-style'). Dubai evidence shows Levantine street-food operators listing sandwich, shawarma, grill and pizza formats on delivery platforms, including a JBR branch on Al Mamsha Street, so Arabic-language naming plus English descriptions fits the observed delivery-menu style.

Abu Dhabi: same core, but plan for a wider family/sharing bias in sizing and a stronger small/large sandwich ladder, following the observed Khalifa City shawarma size ladder and manakish price points (zaatar AED 12, meat manakish AED 22). Consider a manakish or arayes add-on only as a test line - the cited Abu Dhabi listing shows manakish sold there, but it does not show that any Jordanian-style or meat-pizza operator is absent or that customers want this.

Shared localisation items for both cities: halal sourcing and halal labelling stated on the menu; an Arabic-language menu version; a spicy option and a no-pork-by-default kitchen so the same SKU list works in both cities. Do not create separate Dubai and Abu Dhabi recipes at launch - one spec, two price/packaging variants, to keep prep and training simple.

sections.title: Test price bands and how to validate

items.text: Proposed launch test bands (delivery channel, net of tax and discounts, both cities unless noted): kebab sandwich regular AED 22-28, large AED 30-38; meat pizza 8in AED 32-40, 10in AED 48-58, 13in AED 65-80. Anchors: observed Levantine-style sandwich items at AED 11-26 and pizza items at AED 38-40 (Dubai JBR) and AED 33-69 for one UAE chain's 8/10/13in ladder. Bands are proposals, not observed market ranges or margins.

Validate each band against your own costed recipe before publishing: set the portion weight, then price so that food, packaging and platform commission are covered at the tested price. Observed menu prices are not checkout totals - delivery charges, extras and tax treatment were not verified on the cited listings - so treat every citation as a shelf-price anchor only.

assumptions: Business profile: Jordanian restaurant, core products meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches; both cities are targets. No budget, rent budget, branch format, audience, positioning or opening date are set, so this plan is channel-agnostic and assumes delivery-led launch.

All portions, size labels and price bands above are proposals requiring your own weighed specifications and costed recipes; the cited competitor listings did not publish gram weights, pizza diameters, or checkout totals.
next_steps: Weigh and photograph every proposed SKU on a scale, set a written spec sheet (dough ball weight, cooked kebab weight, bread size), and cost each one including packaging before choosing the final prices.

Run a 4-6 week single-city pilot menu first (one city, delivery platforms plus walk-in) with the core 7 SKUs, and add the 13in/10in pizza only if the pilot shows it sells; measure item mix and repeat rate rather than assuming demand.

If you want a break-even check on the pilot, send me eight numbers: average order revenue, food cost per order, packaging per order, other variable cost per order, delivery share (fraction), delivery commission rate (fraction), monthly fixed costs, and operating days per month.
questions: Do you plan a delivery-led launch, a dine-in/small-store format, or both - and roughly what average order value and food-cost percentage are you targeting?
